title: Windows — Windshield Assembly — Install the Drained Corner Bracket and Reseal to the Revised Standard
abstract: Replaces the windshield corner bracket with the drained profile and reseals the frame interface to the revised standard, at the next windshield change, to stop the moisture ingress driving early pane removals.

sections.planning_reason: Windshield removals in the first four years of service ran at three times the predicted rate, and nineteen of twenty-four units examined showed moisture behind the seal at the lower forward corner. The bracket as delivered creates a shallow pocket where water collects during rain and washing, and the original sealant loses adhesion at the pocket edge after repeated thermal cycling. Each removal costs the operator a pane and a day of downtime.
sections.description: This bulletin replaces the corner bracket with the drained profile, replaces the obsolete spar cap at the lower forward corner with the current item and reseals the frame interface to the revised standard with a defined bead profile. The pane and the heating film connections are unchanged. Work is done with the pane out, so the bulletin is normally embodied at a scheduled windshield change.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Remove the windshield to AMM-M-56-10-11-000-045-A and protect the aperture. Remove the corner bracket and the obsolete spar cap, then strip the old sealant from the frame interface and clean to the standard given in the bulletin. Install the current spar cap and the drained bracket, checking that the drain path is open with the supplied gauge. Apply the revised sealant with the bead profile shown, respecting the working life stated on the cartridge. Refit the windshield, respect the full cure time before pressurisation and do a leak check. Do the window heating functional test, then update the parts catalogue effectivity record and make the aircraft records entry.
sections.effectivity_note: Applies to MERIDIAN-42 and MERIDIAN-46 aircraft between MSN M00032 and M00329, excluding MSN M00113 which received the post modification standard on the assembly line. Aircraft with existing corner corrosion identified by MRD-56-1013 must have that finding dispositioned before this bulletin is embodied.
sections.material_note: Kit is per side and contains the drained bracket, the spar cap, the tension head bolt set and two sealant cartridges. The removed bracket is returned for credit. Sealant has a nine month shelf life at five degrees and must be conditioned before use.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next windshield replacement, or within 60 months of the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.
